objectClass.notes: Observed from front, side, top, and detail close-ups. Bilaterally symmetric hull with asymmetric deck fittings. Intended as a playable real-time browser vessel, not a manufacturing-grade naval-architecture mesh.

reasoning: The lofted hull, sheer line, keel, deck opening, and rail profile control the silhouette from three orthographic views.
Identity depends on separate mast, boom, two sails, standing/running rigging, cabin, helm, lamps, life ring, fenders, cleats, and anchor fittings.
Close-ups expose wood joinery, rope lay, canvas seams, painted-plank seams, metal wear, glass emission, and edge weathering.
Gameplay requires named pivots, sockets, collider intent, and compatibility with the existing Rapier rigid-body root.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Choose simple/moderate/complex/ultra-complex from observed structure, not from a hardcoded domain.

unknownsToResolveBeforeImplementation: The underwater keel cross-section and hull underside are inferred from the side/front silhouettes; confidence 0.70.
Port-side fittings not visible in the side close-up are mirrored only where the top view supports symmetry; confidence 0.78.
Below-deck interior and cabin interior are hidden and will remain unmodeled except for dark cavity backing.
Exact historical rig classification and rope routing are approximated to the visible two-sail arrangement rather than claimed as naval-architecture accuracy.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: Horizontal plank seams across the white and blue painted hull bands
Irregular blue and white paint loss exposing warmer wood along plank edges and bow/stern
Thin red-brown anti-fouling separator between white topside and blue lower hull
Raised varnished wood rail following the full sheer line
Longitudinal deck planks with darker caulk gaps and cross joints
Directional timber grain with lighter worn edges on deck, cabin, mast, boom, and helm
Curved horizontal sail panel seams and reinforced perimeter hems
Warm grey weathering concentrated along sail seams, corners, and lower edges
Helical strand relief on standing rigging, coiled lines, and bollard wraps
Eight radial wooden wheel spokes with central metal hub and hand-worn rim
Alternating off-white and red-orange life-ring quadrants with four rope retainers
Warm amber lantern bulb inside blackened metal frame and clear glass enclosure
Two circular dark glass portholes with raised brass/wood rims on cabin side
Paired cleats and bollards with raised metal bases, rope wraps, and attachment bolts
White anchor emblem on the blue forked masthead flag

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: At 4.35 m length and 1.58 m beam, front/side/top renders preserve the reference hull sheer, rounded beam, pointed bow, transom taper, waterline, and mast-to-hull proportions.
The model includes separate action-ready hull, keel, deck, cabin, mast/boom, main sail, jib, rigging, helm/rudder, lamp, life-ring, fender, cleat, bollard, anchor, and masthead flag assemblies.

Neutral and grazing renders distinguish varnished timber, weathered blue/white marine paint, aged canvas, laid rope, metal hardware, and emissive/transmissive lantern glass without reusing PBR channels.
All visible appendages overlap or embed at named sockets; the visual root remains compatible with the existing Rapier BoatRoot transform and LOD system.
A front, starboard side, top, three-quarter bow, and three-quarter stern review shows no flat-card hull, floating fittings, collapsed sails, or missing identity systems.

featureGroups.name: Lofted hull, keel, sheer and painted bands
qualityCriteria: Hull is a closed continuous loft, not a box stack or flat extrusion.
Side length:beam proportion is 4.35:1.58; bow is fine and elevated, stern is rounded/tapered.
White topside, red-brown waterline, and deep blue lower planks follow the reference.

featureGroups.name: Mast, boom, two sails and rigging
qualityCriteria: Mast height and sail triangle proportions match the dimensioned views.
Main sail and jib have thickness, camber, panel seams, hems, and credible root attachments.
Standing and running rigging visibly connect masthead, boom, bow, stern, and gunwale sockets.
failureModes: single generic sail replacing the two-sail silhouette

featureGroups.name: Planked deck, gunwale and twin-porthole cabin
qualityCriteria: Top-view footprint includes the open cockpit, central cabin/companionway, longitudinal plank layout, and curved rails.
Cabin carries two circular portholes and a raised hatch with visible bevels.

featureGroups.name: Helm, rudder, lamps, life ring and hardware
qualityCriteria: Eight-spoke helm, stern rudder, framed amber lamps, quadrant life ring, cleats, bollard, fenders, and anchor are separately named and clickable.
Repeated fittings use shared geometry/material systems with reference-supported placement.

featureGroups.name: Independent marine PBR material response
qualityCriteria: Wood grain direction follows component axes with separate roughness and height signals.
Paint edge wear exposes warm timber; sail stains follow seams; rope relief reads at grazing light.
Metal, canvas, paint, wood, rope, and glass remain distinct under neutral relighting.
failureModes: albedo reused as roughness or bump

featureGroups.name: Action-ready attachments and physics compatibility
qualityCriteria: Every mast, boom, sail, rope, helm, rudder, lamp, life ring, cleat, and fender has a parent socket and overlap.
BoatRoot remains the single physics-driven transform; movable helm and rudder have semantic pivots.
sculptRuntime exposes nodes, sockets, collider intent, destruction groups, and clickable named meshes.
failureModes: visual parts use world coordinates and drift from physics root

visualDeltaChecks: front/side/top hull silhouette and 4.35:1.58 proportion delta
mast height, main-sail/jib area, boom length, and rigging negative-space delta
deck opening, cabin, helm, porthole, life-ring, lamp, cleat, fender, and anchor placement delta
blue/white/red-brown paint band coverage and timber/canvas/rope/metal/glass response delta
three-quarter cross-section volume and attachment gap delta
named-part coverage, pivot, socket, collider, and physics-root compatibility delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

authoringInstruction: Fill observed object class, complexity reasoning, featureGroups, visualDeltaChecks, and unknowns before generating or implementing ObjectSculptSpec.
